reasons_add: Al-Sāmarrāʾī completes the comparison: jāʾa suits the deniers' harsher afterlife arrival, with regret and burdens, whereas atā suits a lighter worldly crisis in which God may remove the affliction (6:30–31, 6:40–41). He argues that jāʾa is heavier in sound and says the Qur'an uses only its past form, while atā appears in several conjugations; the heavier form matches the harsher scene.
Burhān also contrasts backs with heads: backs bear weight better.

positions.position: The ending yazirūn echoes awzārahum through paronomasia.
positions.reasons: Burhān identifies the echo as paronomasia.
